title: Variance-adaptive confidence regions for fixed-benchmark binomial mixtures, with application to LLM evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.21266v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We construct confidence intervals for linear functionals $\theta(F_m)=\int h\,dF_m$ of the empirical law $F_m$ of success probabilities $p_1,\dots,p_m$, from independent counts $c_i\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p_i)$, as for a language model run $n$ times per problem. Coverage is at least $1-\alpha$ for every $n$, $m$ and fixed $(p_i)$, simultaneously for all bounded $h$. The variance-adaptive (VA) region tests each candidate mixing law with the conditional variance of the tail counts it implies. This variance is linear in the law, so the region is a linear program, and cell envelopes keep it valid off-grid. Regions calibrated for iid sampling target a super-population law and are conservative for $\theta(F_m)$. With all $n$ tail counts, fixed $n$, continuous $h$ and a grid refined as $m\to\infty$, the identification part of VA's width is first-order worst-case optimal, as for any localization with the same index set. translated_title: 固定基准下二项混合分布的方差自适应置信区域及其在大语言模型评估中的应用
translated_abstract: 我们为成功概率 $p_1,\dots,p_m$ 的经验分布 $F_m$ 的线性泛函 $\theta(F_m)=\int h\,dF_m$ 构造置信区间，数据来自独立计数 $c_i\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p_i)$，例如语言模型在每个问题上运行 $n$ 次的情形。对于任意的 $n$、$m$ 和固定的 $(p_i)$，覆盖率至少为 $1-\alpha$，且对所有有界的 $h$ 同时成立。方差自适应（VA）区域用它所蕴含的尾部计数的条件方差来检验每个候选混合分布。该方差关于分布是线性的，因此该区域可表示为一个线性规划，而胞腔包络使其在网格之外仍然有效。为独立同分布抽样校准的区域针对的是超总体分布，对于 $\theta(F_m)$ 而言是保守的。在利用全部 $n$ 个尾部计数、固定 $n$、连续 $h$ 且网格随 $m\to\infty$ 不断加密的条件下，VA 宽度的识别部分在一阶最坏情形意义上是最优的，与具有相同指标集的任何局部化方法相当。在预先固定的规则下……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出方差自适应（VA）置信区域方法，基于固定基准上的二项计数为经验分布线性泛函构造对任意有界泛函同时具有有限样本覆盖保证的置信区间，其可通过线性规划计算并在一阶最坏情形意义下达到最优宽度，可直接应用于大语言模型评估。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes variance-adaptive (VA) confidence regions for linear functionals of empirical success-probability distributions from binomial counts on a fixed benchmark, achieving finite-sample simultaneous coverage for all bounded functionals, linear-program computability, and first-order worst-case optimal width, with direct application to LLM evaluation.
